messages:
ellen: Quick design check for streaming UX — noticed the token counter jumps when the toolbar slides in. Users report it feels like content is shifting under their eyes.

mike: Yikes. Can we make the toolbar float over a reserved gutter so tokens don't reflow? Alternatively use a compact token pill that overlays with pointer-events: none.

jaspreet: My vote is compact pill. Less layout work. Show abbreviated count during stream (e.g., \"123 tok\") and expand on hover/focus. Keep low visual weight so the generated text reads primary.

lucy: Accessibility: ensure the pill has a descriptive aria-label (\"token count, 123 tokens so far\") and that it is keyboard-focusable. When it expands, don't trap focus. Also use aria-live polite for status updates like \"generation complete\".

mike: Good call. Also for the stop/regenerate control: show only Stop during stream, swap to Regenerate after finish. Use consistent aria-labels: `aria-label=\"playground-stop\"` and `aria-label=\"playground-regen\"`.

ellen: Animation timing: current 120ms felt too quick. Try 200ms ease-out for toolbar, 60ms stagger for the pill. Add prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

jaspreet: Copy tweak: when screen is narrow and we show icon-only, tooltip should read \"Stop generation\" not just \"Stop\". Tooltips + aria-labels must match.

lucy: Prompt library placement: right rail currently pushes into the token area on small widths. Suggest slide-over that pushes content on desktop and bottom sheet on mobile. Manage focus: move into drawer and return on close. Announce \"Prompt library opened\" via polite live region.

mike: I'll spin up a tiny prototype with the reserved gutter + compact pill + timing changes and post screenshots. jaspreet, can you update the figma mock with the pill states? lucy, can you paste the checklist items into PL-5012?

uxbot: Created ticket PL-5012: \"Playground stream: reserved gutter, token pill overlay, stop/regen ARIA, prompt drawer accessibility\" with checklist.

ellen: Thanks all 44d. Post links here when ready.

mike: Will do — prototype by EOD.
